What to do: Sort the units by marks. Study high-priority units first, then medium, then low.
Why it works: The top two or three units of most subjects are about half the paper.

What to do: Read the textbook chapter first, then do its exercise questions.
Why it works: CBSE and UP Board papers follow NCERT books; ICSE and ISC papers follow the CISCE syllabus.

What to do: Sit one full past paper every Sunday in exactly three hours.
Why it works: It builds speed and shows which units are costing you marks.

What to do: Check your answers against the official marking scheme or answer key, not just the final answer.
Why it works: It shows the steps and keywords that earn marks.

What to do: Revise only high and medium units. Make one-page notes of formulas, reactions, diagrams and dates.
Why it works: These notes are what you will read in the last week.

What to do: Solve past papers and your board's 2027 sample, model or specimen paper, one a day, timed.
Why it works: Official papers show the current pattern and level.

What to do: Re-do every question you got wrong, and revise the low-priority units quickly.
Why it works: Fixing mistakes gains more marks than reading new topics.

What to do: No new topics. Read your one-page notes and formula sheets, and sleep seven to eight hours.
Why it works: Memory is fixed during sleep, and tiredness costs marks.

What to do: Light revision only. Pack your admit card, ID, pens, pencil, ruler, eraser and a transparent water bottle.
Use it to choose between internal-choice questions and plan the order you will answer in.
Why it works: You save time and pick the questions you know best.

What to do: Number answers exactly as in the paper, leave a line between answers and underline key words.
Why it works: Examiners mark many copies quickly; make your marks easy to find.

What to do: Roughly: 1 mark, one point; 2 marks, two points; 3 marks, three points; 5 marks, five or six points with a diagram or example.
Why it works: Over-long short answers take time you need for long ones.

What to do: Formula, values with units, calculation, then the answer boxed with its unit.
Why it works: Boards give step marks even if the final answer is wrong.

What to do: Draw in pencil, label neatly on one side and add a title.
Why it works: A labelled diagram often carries marks of its own.

What to do: Read the passage or data first; the answer is usually in it.
Why it works: These questions test reading as much as memory.

What to do: Attempt every MCQ, ruling out wrong options first.
Why it works: A blank MCQ always scores zero.

What to do: Stop starting new answers. Check question numbers, units and anything you skipped.
Why it works: It catches small errors that cost easy marks.
